penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Operating a real-device farm requires physical hardware procurement, maintenance, and on-site management — per-customer delivery is inherently hardware-bound and cannot be automated by Claude.

penalties_applied.name: requires_physical_logistics
penalties_applied.reason: The core value proposition (real physical devices) requires procuring, racking, maintaining, and retiring physical mobile devices — logistics Claude cannot handle.

rationale: The buyer is clear and the willingness-to-pay signal is genuine — dev/QA leads at startups already pay for CI/CD and testing tooling, and one commenter explicitly stated they'd pay for managed real-device testing. However, the product's entire value proposition rests on physical device infrastructure: buying, provisioning, maintaining, and replacing real iOS/Android handsets. That is irreducibly hardware-bound logistics that a solo non-technical operator running a Claude factory cannot automate or delegate away. Buildability and operational autonomy both score 1 because no amount of AI prompting replaces a device lab.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator could NOT realistically build and maintain this. The competitive advantage — real device access — requires physical hardware management (sourcing, racking, replacing broken devices, managing iOS/Android OS updates on physical units). This is infrastructure-company territory (AWS Device Farm, BrowserStack, Sauce Labs all have significant hardware ops teams). Attempting this as a one-person factory-backed micro-service would result in a hardware ops nightmare before the first paying customer. Recommend dropping entirely and redirecting to software-only testing tooling if the QA space is appealing.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 1, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (scored 1, floor is 6). Physical device farm is not buildable with Claude + prompts + Stripe. Drop is correct regardless of total.
